redFirst.basis: mode regression, expectRedFirst false; the failure reproduces only on windows-latest (read-only git loose objects), not on this darwin host

outcome.technical: Sole creator of stamp-derive-* is test_stamp_verification.py (sr213 block, tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='stamp-derive-')), which builds a git repo and removed it with shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True). Git writes loose objects read-only; Windows refuses to unlink read-only files (documented in _output.remove_tree's docstring), so the removal failed silently and, with TMPDIR==cwd under the sweep, left the dir in the watched cwd. Fix: use _harness.remove_tree (rmtree, then chmod pass, then rmtree; returns whether the tree is gone) and new case sr214 asserts it returned True, the path is gone, and no stamp-derive-* sibling remains in the directory it was made in (the cwd under the sweep) - on every OS. Selftest: 264/264 passed. stamp-verification.py unchanged (no need). Not run: full sweep (Windows-only behaviour cannot be reproduced on darwin).
outcome.descriptive: The red-first suite's git fixture is now removed with the read-only-tolerant helper and the removal is asserted, so no stamp-derive directory survives on Windows.

testsAdded: sr214 the derive fixture leaves nothing behind
